microtopics.title: Conformational torsion and p-orbital alignment
microtopics.badge_reason: Learners must track 3D orbital vectors under dihedral rotation and distinguish symmetry overlap from electron count.
entry_assumptions: Understands sigma and pi bonding as head-on and lateral orbital overlaps.
Can recognize parallel versus perpendicular geometric vectors in 3D.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Delocalisation requires continuous, parallel alignment of unhybridised p orbitals; twisting the molecular framework breaks orbital overlap by symmetry orthogonality, converting a delocalised pi system into localized fragments without changing formal electron count.

teaching_path.action: Inspect the planar ground state and identify parallel p-orbital alignment across adjacent atoms.
teaching_path.why_valid: Maximum lateral overlap occurs when p-orbital axes are strictly parallel (theta = 0°).

teaching_path.action: Apply a dihedral twist about the connecting sigma bond and evaluate the overlap integral.
teaching_path.why_valid: Overlap scales with the cosine of the twist angle theta, diminishing as rotation progresses.

teaching_path.action: Demonstrate complete orthogonality at 90 degrees: overlap vanishes while formal electron count and atom connectivity remain unchanged.
teaching_path.why_valid: A p orbital perpendicular to an adjacent pi system lies entirely in its nodal plane, yielding zero net overlap integral.

teaching_path.action: Distinguish qualitative model assumptions from measured physical observables.
teaching_path.why_valid: Rotational barrier and bond lengths are measurable physical quantities; hybrid orbitals and single-parameter overlap terms are localized model approximations.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The hybridisation label changes, so donation disappears (confusing naming with physical causation).
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does swapping a human hybridisation label physically cause electrons to stop overlapping, or does geometric orientation determine overlap?
misconceptions.repair: Physical geometric alignment and overlap integral determine delocalisation; hybridisation labels describe rather than cause bonding behavior.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Twisting a bond alters the formal electron count or breaks the sigma framework.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: When the amino group twists by 90 degrees, do any sigma bonds break or do valence electrons disappear?
misconceptions.repair: Torsion rotates orbital vectors in space; atom connectivity and formal electron counts remain strictly invariant.

exit_task.prompt: An allyl cation, [CH2=CH–CH2]+, is twisted by 90 degrees about one of its C–C bonds. What happens to the overlap between the twisted CH2 p orbital and the adjacent pi system, and how does the formal electron count change? Explain before calculating.

answer.summary: Orbital overlap between the twisted CH2 group and the adjacent pi bond drops to zero due to symmetry orthogonality; the formal electron count (2 pi electrons in the remaining double bond, vacant p orbital on the twisted carbon) remains strictly invariant.
reasoning: Rotation by 90 degrees places the terminal p orbital in the nodal plane of the adjacent pi system, extinguishing lateral overlap.
Total valence electrons and sigma bond connectivity are unchanged by conformational rotation.
answer.check: Verify symmetry: the twisted p orbital is perpendicular to the adjacent p orbitals, giving zero net overlap integral.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task assesses qualitative understanding of orbital alignment and orthogonality.

microtopics.research_contribution: Issue #38 benchmark questions cluster Q1, Q2, Q3, and Q9 around conformational torsion, orbital overlap, and the boundaries of hybridisation models.

predict.prompt: When an amide bond twists toward 90 degrees, does resonance donation increase, decrease, or remain constant?
predict.defensible_answer: Resonance donation decreases and vanishes at 90 degrees due to the loss of parallel p-orbital overlap.

attempt.produces: An orbital alignment explanation and orthogonality proof.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that lateral p overlap requires parallel alignment and vanishes at 90 degrees.
Preserves electron count and connectivity invariants.

accepted: Overlap scales as cos(theta) and vanishes at 90° because the p orbitals become mutually perpendicular; electron count is unchanged.
rejected: Donation disappears because the hybridisation label changed.

boundary_test.prompt: If the amide is locked into a rigid bicyclic bridgehead where nitrogen is twisted 90 degrees (anti-Bredt amide), would you expect normal amide properties?
boundary_test.answer: No; with zero orbital overlap, the nitrogen behaves like a normal basic amine and the carbonyl behaves like a reactive ketone.
boundary_test.confirms: Demonstrates that physical orbital overlap governs chemical reactivity, not the presence of N and C=O atoms in the formula.

construction_units.decision: Relate dihedral twist angle to orbital overlap loss, demonstrate zero overlap at 90 degrees, and separate model assumptions from physical facts

independent_checks.statement: CHECK: Show why S(90°) = 0 by p-orbital symmetry without calculating.

microtopics.title: Delocalisation-sensitive hybridisation boundaries
microtopics.badge_reason: Requires reconciling local electron-domain counting with adjacent pi conjugation driving rehybridisation.
entry_assumptions: Can determine local Lewis structures and count electron domains.
Understands resonance stabilization in introductory conjugated systems.
microtopics.inferential_jump: When an unshared electron pair can participate in resonance delocalisation with an adjacent pi system, the atom rehybridises (typically to sp2) to place the pair in an unhybridised p orbital, overriding naive 4-domain sp3 predictions.

teaching_path.action: Count local sigma bonds and lone pairs to establish baseline domain count.
teaching_path.why_valid: Steric number provides an initial geometry estimate for isolated atoms.

teaching_path.action: Check for adjacent pi bonds, vacant p orbitals, or radical centers capable of resonance delocalisation.
teaching_path.why_valid: Resonance delocalisation requires contiguous atoms with available p orbitals.

teaching_path.action: Select rehybridised sp2 framework if resonance stabilization energy exceeds the rehybridisation promotion energy.
teaching_path.why_valid: Minimizing total molecular electronic energy determines equilibrium geometry.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Four electron domains always forces sp3 hybridization and pyramidal shape.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If an atom has 4 domains but is adjacent to a C=O pi bond, can delocalisation change its preferred hybridisation?
misconceptions.repair: Delocalisation stabilization can favor rehybridisation to sp2 with a lone pair in an unhybridised p orbital.

exit_task.prompt: Explain why the nitrogen in aniline (C6H5–NH2) is nearly planar rather than strongly pyramidal as in ammonia.

answer.summary: The nitrogen lone pair delocalises into the aromatic pi system of the benzene ring, which requires an aligned p-like orbital on nitrogen; this resonance stabilization favors an approximately planar sp2-like geometry over a localized pyramidal sp3 state.
reasoning: The benzene ring has a continuous cyclic pi system of parallel p orbitals.
Rehybridising toward sp2 allows the nitrogen lone pair to achieve parallel overlap with the ring pi system.
answer.check: Verify that resonance contributors place negative formal charge on the ortho and para positions of the ring.

microtopics.research_contribution: Addresses Q1, Q5, Q7, and Q8.

predict.prompt: Will formamide nitrogen be pyramidal like ammonia or planar like an sp2 carbon?
predict.defensible_answer: Planar, because lone pair delocalisation into the carbonyl pi system provides significant resonance stabilization.

rubric.criterion: Explains why sp2 is preferred over sp3

accepted: sp2 framework with lone pair in pz
rejected: strictly sp3 because steric number is 4

microtopics.title: Local domain counting versus conjugated networks
microtopics.badge_reason: Distinguishes through-bond continuous conjugation from isolated saturated spacers and orthogonal pi networks.
entry_assumptions: Understands orbital hybridisation in alkanes and alkenes.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Pi delocalisation strictly requires contiguous atoms with unhybridised p orbitals; a saturated sp3 atom with four sigma bonds interrupts the pi highway, enforcing localized domain behavior.

teaching_path.action: Trace the bonding sequence across adjacent atoms.
teaching_path.why_valid: Continuous orbital overlap requires an unbroken chain of adjacent p-bearing centers.

teaching_path.action: Identify any intervening saturated sp3 atoms lacking unhybridised p orbitals.
teaching_path.why_valid: A saturated node has all valence orbitals engaged in sigma bonds, blocking lateral pi overlap.

teaching_path.action: Apply localized counting where pathways are broken, and conjugated models where pathways are continuous.
teaching_path.why_valid: Assigns appropriate physical models based on orbital connectivity.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Spatial proximity in a folded chain allows pi conjugation across saturated spacers.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Can a lone pair conjugate through a saturated -CH2- carbon if the chain folds?
misconceptions.repair: Conjugation requires continuous through-bond alignment of unhybridised p orbitals; through-space proximity does not form a pi bond.

exit_task.prompt: Compare the nitrogen in benzylamine (C6H5–CH2–NH2) with aniline (C6H5–NH2). Which one is more basic, and why?

answer.summary: Benzylamine is much more basic (similar to aliphatic amines) because the intervening saturated –CH2– carbon has four sigma bonds and no unhybridised p orbital, insulating the nitrogen lone pair from the aromatic pi system; in aniline, the nitrogen is directly bonded to the ring and its lone pair is delocalised.
reasoning: The –CH2– group in benzylamine acts as an electronic insulator.
Delocalisation in aniline lowers the electron density on nitrogen, greatly reducing basicity.
answer.check: pKa of benzylammonium is ~9.3, whereas anilinium is ~4.6.

rejected: both have carbonyls so both delocalise

relations.meaning: Lateral orbital overlap between two unhybridised p orbitals depends on the cosine of their dihedral alignment angle theta.

symbols.meaning: maximum overlap integral at parallel coplanar alignment
dihedral twist angle about internuclear axis

conditions: Applies to lateral overlap between two p orbitals rotated about their connecting sigma internuclear axis.
At theta = 90°, S = 0 by symmetry orthogonality.

derivation.action: Define p-orbital wavefunctions with orientation vectors in cylindrical/spherical coordinates.
derivation.why_valid: Directional p orbitals transform as Cartesian vector components.

derivation.action: Apply rotation operator around the internuclear z-axis by angle theta.
derivation.why_valid: Rotation projects the p-orbital into parallel and perpendicular components.

derivation.action: Integrate product over all space: perpendicular term integrates to zero, leaving cos(theta) scaling.
derivation.why_valid: Symmetry orthogonality extinguishes the out-of-plane component.

limits: Model assumes rigid nuclear framework and isolated two-orbital interaction.
Total molecular energy does not scale as cos(theta) due to sigma strain and perturbation quadratic energy scaling.
checks: Verify boundary conditions: S(0°) = S_0; S(90°) = 0; S(180°) = -S_0.

relations.expression: n \text{ atomic orbitals} \to n \text{ hybrid/molecular orbitals}
relations.meaning: Linear combination of atomic orbitals preserves basis dimensionality: combining s and two p orbitals produces three sp2 hybrids and leaves one unhybridised p orbital.

symbols.meaning: number of atomic basis orbitals combined

conditions: Conservation of orbital dimensionality under unitary transformations.
Valence bond hybridisation creates directed equivalent orbitals for sigma bonding while leaving remaining p orbitals for pi delocalisation.

derivation.action: Set up orthonormal basis of one 2s and three 2p orbitals (n=4).
derivation.why_valid: Valence shell has 4 independent spatial wavefunctions.

derivation.action: Construct unitary transformation mixing 2s with 2px and 2py.
derivation.why_valid: Unitary mixing preserves total number of orthogonal states.
derivation.output: three sp2 hybrids + one unhybridised pz

derivation.action: Verify normalization and mutual orthogonality of all 4 resulting orbitals.
derivation.why_valid: Ensures mathematical completeness and probability conservation.

limits: Hybrid orbitals are mathematical basis choices, not independent physical observables.
Real molecules can exhibit fractional hybridization (e.g. sp^2.2).
checks: Sum of s and p fractional characters equals 1.0 for each hybrid and sums to the basis orbital count.

relations.meaning: Continuous pi delocalisation requires non-zero pairwise overlap along every adjacent step of the pathway; an intervening saturated sp3 atom lacks unhybridised p orbitals and interrupts the conjugation highway.

symbols.meaning: unhybridised p orbital at atom i

conditions: All atoms in the conjugated network must have unhybridised p orbitals.
Adjacent p orbitals must have coplanar symmetry alignment.

derivation.action: Define molecular orbital as linear combination of p orbitals across all contiguous atoms.
derivation.why_valid: Hückel and MO theory construct delocalised wavefunctions from adjacent p overlaps.

derivation.action: Evaluate resonance integral beta between adjacent atoms i and i+1.
derivation.why_valid: Resonance integral beta is proportional to overlap integral <p_i | p_{i+1}>.

derivation.action: If any node has all valence orbitals in sigma bonds, beta vanishes, decoupling the secular determinant into isolated blocks.
derivation.why_valid: Zero overlap at an intervening node blocks through-bond electron delocalisation.

limits: Through-space (homoconjugation) interactions are negligible compared to direct through-bond conjugation in standard aliphatic spacers.
checks: Verify that converting intervening -CH2- to -CH=CH- restores non-zero resonance integral across the chain.

demand_dimensions.model_choice: Choose between localized sp3, planar sp2 with unhybridised p, or orthogonal pi models.
demand_dimensions.representation_translation: Translate verbal formulas and conformations into 3D orbital alignments and nodal planes.
demand_dimensions.reasoning_steps: Local count, adjacency check, overlap symmetry evaluation, energy and model boundary check.
demand_dimensions.novelty: Amide delocalisation, 90-degree torsional decoupling, methyl radical SOMO, and allene orthogonal pi bonds.

safe_variations: Change substituents while preserving the same orbital alignment and conjugation conditions.
transfer_boundaries: Do not equate spatial proximity with through-bond conjugation.
Do not treat hybridisation as a physical cause of bond angles or reactivity.
common_wrong_routes: Apply four domains therefore sp3 automatically without checking adjacent pi systems.
Assume twisting breaks formal electron counts or chemical connectivity.
